title: Rat Chromaffin cells primary cultures: Standardization and quality assessment for single-cell assays
protocol: Prepare the dissociation solution containing 2.6 mg/ml collagenase type I, 3 mg/ml BSA, 0.15 mg/ml DNase I, and 0.15 mg/ml hyaluronidase I-S in HBSS.
Keep the dissociation solution at room temperature.
Treat coverslips with 0.1 mg/ml poly-D-lysine for one hour.
Rinse the treated coverslips thoroughly.
Sacrifice animals according to institutionally approved ethical procedures without stressing them.
Extract adrenal glands immediately after sacrifice and place on ice-cold HBSS supplemented with antibiotics.
Perform a medial laparotomy to access both adrenal glands adequately.
Under a dissection stereomicroscope, remove adipose tissue surrounding the gland using a stainless steel scalpel blade.
Decapsulate the adrenal glands carefully.
Remove the adrenal cortex to isolate medullary tissue.
Handle the gland carefully to avoid crushing it.
Keep the tissue wet with cold HBSS during handling to preserve it and facilitate removal of fatty tissue.
Collect adrenal medullas in a tube containing cold HBSS.
Drop 3 ml of dissociation solution in the lid of a small culture dish.
Place the medullas into the dissociation solution and cut each into four pieces.
Transfer the medulla chunks and solution to a Falcon tube using a glass Pasteur pipette with a fire-polished broad tip.
Place the tube in a thermostatic bath at 37°C for enzymatic digestion (25-30 min).
Gently resuspend the solution every 10 minutes during digestion.
Resuspend continuously over the last 5 minutes until medullary tissue is no longer visible by eye.
Add cold HBSS to stop the enzymatic reaction, reaching a final volume of 10 ml.
Place the tube containing digested tissue in the rotor of a pre-cooled (4°C) refrigerated centrifuge.
Spin at 800 rpm for 10 minutes.
Discard the supernatant by decanting and resuspend the pellet with 0.8 ml of pre-warmed DMEM+10% FCS and antibiotics.
Add 1 or 2 drops on each poly-D-lysine-treated coverslip.
Allow the cells to settle down for 1 hour inside a cell incubator at 37°C.
Refill the culture dish with 1-1.5 ml of DMEM+10% FCS.
Incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Replace the medium 24 hours later.
Repeat replacing the medium every 48 hours thereafter.
Stain the cells with trypan blue solution (0.2%) for viability assessment.
Count the cells in a hemocytometer chamber to estimate yield and cellular viability.
Label cells with fluorescein diacetate (FDA, 0.12 uM) for an alternative viability test using flow cytometry.
Stain cells with neutral red to estimate purity of chromaffin cell cultures.
Evaluate the functional viability of the cells through various assays such as autofluorescence measurements.
Measure fluorimetric cytosolic Ca<sup>2+</sup> levels (basal or increments evoked by high K<sup>+</sup> containing solutions or acetylcholine [ACh] signals).
Conduct electrophysiological recordings of ACh-activated currents to assess cell function.
